paper.title: An Asymptotically Optimal Primal-Dual Incremental Algorithm for Contextual Linear Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual linear bandit (CLB) with finite contexts drawn i.i.d. from rho and finite arms
unmapped: Finite context set X with i.i.d. context distribution rho, rho(x) >= rho_min > 0 for all x
Features phi(x,a) bounded by L in l2 norm; parameter set Theta compact with ||theta|| <= B (B and L used by the algorithm)
Per-context action set is fixed finite set A; the effective feature set varies with the observed context
settings.definition_quote: At each time step $t \in \mathbb{N}$, the learner observes a context $X_t\in\X$ drawn i.i.d.\ from a context distribution $\rho$, it pulls an arm $A_t\in\A$, and it receives a reward $Y_{t} = \phi(X_t,A_t)^\transp\theta^\star + \xi_t$ ... where $\xi \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2)$ is a Gaussian noise. Assumption 1: ... $\|\theta\|_2 \leq B$ ... $\| \phi(x,a) \|_2 \leq L$ ... $\rho(x) \geq \rho_{\min} > 0$ ... unique optimal arm in each context.

symbols.C_lin: v*(theta*), value of the contextual linear lower-bound optimisation problem (P)

extra_assumptions: beta_{t-1}=c_{n,1/n}, gamma_t=c_{n,1/S_t^2}, z_k=z_0 e^k, p_k=z_k e^{2k}, step sizes 1/sqrt(p_k)

source.label: thm:regret.bound
source.quote: If \algo is run with confidence values $\beta_{t-1} = c_{n,1/n}$ and $\gamma_t = c_{n,1/S_t^2}$ ... learning rates $\alpha_k^\lambda = \alpha_k^\omega = 1/\sqrt{p_k}$ and increasing sequences $z_k = z_0 e^k$ and $p_k = z_k e^{2k}$, for some $z_0 \geq 1$, then it is \textbf{asymptotically optimal} with the same constant as in the lower bound of Prop.~\ref{p:lower.bound}.

results.notes: Asymptotic optimality stated qualitatively; encoded as limsup of regret/log n <= v*.

symbols.c_n: c_{n,1/n} = O(log n + d log log n), confidence radius from Theorem 1
symbols.C_const: v* B^2 L^2/sigma^2 + lin_{>=0}(L, B, z_0 (z_underline/z_0)^3, (z_bar/z_0)^2)

source.label: eq:regret.bound.finite
source.quote: Furthermore, for any finite $n$ the regret of \algo is bounded as $\E_{\xi,\rho}^\pi [ R_n(\theta^\star) ] \leq v^\star(\theta^\star) \frac{c_{n,1/n}}{2\sigma^2} + C_{\log} (\log\log n)^{\frac{1}{2}}(\log n)^{\frac{3}{4}} + C_{\mathrm{const}}$

results.notes: Constants C_log and C_const only given as linear-type functions; declared as symbols.

bound.regime: any n; p_k = e^{rk}, r >= 1, z_k arbitrary

source.label: th:worst-case
source.quote: Let $z_k$ be arbitrary, $p_k = e^{rk}$ for some constant $r \geq 1$, and the other parameters be the same as in Thm.~\ref{thm:regret.bound}. Then, for any $n$ the regret of \algo is bounded as $\E[R_n] \leq 12BL\pi^2C_{\lambda_{\max}} + \frac{2e^r(\lambda_{\max}^2 + \log|\A|)}{r}\sqrt{n} + C_{\mathrm{sqrt}} C_{\lambda_{\max}}\log (n) \sqrt{dn}$

results.notes: B mapped to S, L to L_feat, |A| to K, n to T.

source.label: th:worst-case
source.quote: More precisely, the bound is $\wt{\mathcal{{O}}}((\sqrt{d} + |\X|)\sqrt{dn} + \log|\A|\sqrt{n})$, which matches the minimax optimal rate apart from the dependence on $|\X|$

results.notes: Simplified form of Theorem 3 stated in text after the theorem; M_ctx = |X|.

cited_results.cited_title: Minimal exploration in structured stochastic bandits
cited_results.setting_description: Contextual linear bandit with finite contexts/arms, Gaussian noise, uniformly good strategies (also attributed to Lai & Robbins 1985 and Ok et al. 2018)
